mechanism_narrative: The recent drop in WORKPLACES mobility indicates fewer commuting trips and weaker weekday downtown footfall, but because the decline is slowing while transit remains deeply suppressed, the next four weeks should still show a modest recovery in retail visits as residents substitute local errands for work-linked trips.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week average over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing to improve or flatten.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility falls while GROCERY_PHARM rises, households are leaving home for short local trips instead of discretionary home-stay, which should lift retail-and-recreation visits within the next one to two weeks through more neighborhood shopping and errand chaining.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 2 points week-on-week while GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after a week in which RESIDENTIAL drops and GROCERY_PHARM rises by the stated amounts.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT from its very depressed level is a leading signal of relaxed movement constraints and stronger access to shopping districts, so retail-and-recreation mobility should rise over the next four weeks after the transit trough passes.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases by at least 3 points week-on-week from a level below -65
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the next 28 days after TRANSIT rises from below -65 by at least 3 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PARKS mobility relative to the prior two weeks signals warmer-weather leisure substitution away from indoor retail, which should depress retail-and-recreation mobility over the next month as households allocate discretionary trips to outdoor recreation instead of shopping.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while PARKS remains above its last-4-week average.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise together, commuting-linked shopping trips expand faster than either signal alone implies, producing higher retail-and-recreation mobility within four weeks because more workers pass through retail corridors on the way to and from work.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT trend upward together for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in GROCERY_PHARM without a matching rise in WORKPLACES reflects short, necessity-based trips that displace discretionary shopping, so retail-and-recreation mobility should soften within one week of the spike and remain weaker over the next month.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 2 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES does not rise
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within 7 days after a week in which GROCERY_PHARM jumps by at least 2 points and WORKPLACES does not improve.

mechanism_narrative: As soon as TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both recover from their recent lows, the city is transitioning into a reopening regime in which access constraints ease; retail mobility should then rise over the following two weeks because shopping trips piggyback on commuting corridors.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise week-on-week after being below -65 and -35 respectively
evidence_refs: fact:both series are improving from deeply negative levels in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within 14 days after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES post week-on-week gains from the stated low levels.

mechanism_narrative: In a holiday-shopping regime, rising PARKS mobility alongside falling RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates more out-of-home leisure and errands, which should push retail-and-recreation mobility higher over the next four weeks as discretionary outings expand.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week average over the next 28 days when PARKS rises and RESIDENTIAL falls together.
